headline: A 2001 order by President Clinton lifted some US sanctions on Yugoslavia (Serbia and Montenegro) and changed others.
what_it_does: This executive order ended some earlier US restrictions on the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, which then included Serbia and Montenegro. It also changed some of the restrictions that stayed in place. The title does not say which measures were lifted or how the rest were changed.

who_it_affects.group: US businesses and individuals dealing with Yugoslavia
who_it_affects.how: Some earlier limits on trade or financial dealings with the country were lifted or changed.

who_it_affects.group: The government and people of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
who_it_affects.how: Some US sanctions aimed at the country were removed, while others were modified.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed January 17, 2001; the exact effective date is not given in the provided material.
